newsitem.title: USA: USDA buys 7.3 mln lbs beef for school lunches.
newsitem.headline: USDA buys 7.3 mln lbs beef for school lunches.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Tuesday it purchased 7.3 million lbs of frozen beef and beef special trim for the national school lunch program and other federal food assistance programs.
The agency's Agricultural Marketing Service said the beef cost between $0.95 and $1.05 per lb, and will be shipped August 4-29.
The 7.3 million lbs of meat were sold to USDA by Aksarben Foods Inc of Omaha, Neb; Bauer Meat Co of Ocala, Fla;Fresno Meat Co of Fresno, Calif. and Supreme Beef Processors of Dallas.
USDA also said it invited offers to sell frozen ground beef to the agency, but did not identify how much it planned to purchase.
